scope: Actual pinned Synapse v1.164.1 room-version-12 creation, canonical-alias replay and partial-state repair
observations: Creating a private, non-federated room can invite a deterministic local HRIS Matrix user before its first provider login; later JWT login and repeated join succeed. No placeholder peer device or private key is required.
Repeating createRoom with the same canonical alias returns HTTP 400 M_ROOM_IN_USE; resolving the alias returns the same room before and after provider restart.
Immutable creation marker and room version, encryption algorithm, joined history visibility, invite-only join policy and forbidden guest access are readable and match expected state.

An ordinary peer cannot invite additional users or replace the encryption state at power level zero. Room-version-12 creator authority remains privileged; HRIS gateway must mediate creator state/membership controls too.

Deliberately invalid initial power levels fail createRoom with HTTP 400 after reserving its alias and persisting creation/member events. Encryption state is absent. Repeating createRoom cannot finish it because the alias already exists.

The correct creator can verify the retained immutable marker and repair the partial room by setting bounded expected power/encryption/join/history/guest state. Each final state matches its expected content.
limits: Provider control semantics, not cryptographic message/media acceptance; no SDK encrypted payload or HRIS room-publication worker is exercised here.

Alias lookup alone is not admission or proof of complete creation. Production must verify immutable creator/marker, reject alien/mismatching state, reconcile exact membership and recheck HRIS authority before publishing its room binding.
No generic Matrix proxy, new public route, deployment, phone action, real employee message or Starter port. Fixtures own and close their provider process/network and HTTP client.
